blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: In film editing, every frame matters. While macro, content-level edits shape the high-level narrative of a film, small local edits often control timing and direct visual attention. For example, editors can adjust the precise timing of clips to control the length of a meaningful silence, or cut to shots that highlight a specific character's reactions to important moments. These small, detailed edits are slow and tedious to make in standard editing tools because users have to map high-level narrative goals to low-level frame-by-frame adjustments. At the same time, these fine-scale adjustments, which we call micro-edits, can be nuanced and expressive, with different choices serving different creative goals. In this work, we start by conducting a formative study with professional editors to understand the structure of micro-edits and how they are used. We then derive a mathematical formalization for this structure to develop tools that leverage AI and optimization to make exploring micro-edits simpler and more efficient for users. Finally, we validate our tools in multiple user studies and a wide range of video examples.
blocks.zh: 在电影编辑中,每个帧都很重要. 虽然宏观,内容层面的编辑会塑造出一部电影的高层次叙事,但小的局部编辑往往会控制时间,并引导视觉关注. 例如,编辑可以调整剪辑的准确时间来控制有意义的沉默的长度,或者剪接到突出特定人物对重要时刻的反应的镜头. 这些小而详细的编辑方式在标准编辑工具中是缓慢而乏味的,因为用户必须将高层次的叙事目标映射到低层次的逐帧调整. 同时,这些细微的尺度调整,我们称之为"微版",可以细微而有表现力,不同的选择服务于不同的创造性目标. 在这部作品中,我们首先与专业编辑进行成形研究,以了解微编辑的结构以及如何使用. 然后我们为这个结构得出一个数学形式化,以开发出能利用AI和优化的工具来使探索微编辑器对用户更加简单和高效. 最后,我们在多个用户研究和各种视频实例中验证我们的工具。

blocks.en: 1. Introduction
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 导言

blocks.en:
Video editing happens at multiple temporal scales, and editors tend to work in a coarse-to-fine manner. At the coarse scale, they begin with what we call macro-edits , which determine the selection and ordering of video clips. Macro-edits establish a basic timeline to create what is commonly referred to as a rough cut ( O’Steen, 2009 ) . While novice filmmakers and AI-based editing tools often limit editing to rough cuts, skilled filmmakers typically make additional fine-scale edits by decoupling audio and visual transitions and shifting them along a given timeline to control pacing and direct audience attention. These fine-scale edits, which we call micro-edits , offer significant expressive control over a scene’s narrative ( Chandler, 2012 ; Murch, 2025 ) .
However, they require expertise to execute well and remain tedious even for skilled editors ( Dmytryk et al., 2018 ) .
In this work, we address these challenges by developing new interactive tools to make micro-edits easier to explore and apply, focusing on dialogue scenes, which are especially common in narrative film ( Cutting, 2021 ) . Our work comprises four parts:
blocks.zh:
视频编辑发生在多时间尺度上,编辑往往以粗糙到精细的方式工作. 在粗糙的尺度上,它们从我们所谓的宏编辑开始,它决定了视频片段的选择和订购. Macro-edits为创建通称"粗剪"(O ' Steen,2009)设定了基本时间表. 虽然新颖的电影制片人和基于AI的编辑工具往往将编辑限制在粗略的剪接上,但熟练的电影制作人通常通过将音频和视觉的过渡脱钩来进行额外的精细尺度的编辑,并沿着特定的时间线进行转换来控制速度并引导观众关注. 这些精细的编辑,我们称之为"微编辑"(micro-edits),对一个场景的叙事提供了显著的表达性控制(Chandler,2012;Murch,2025).
然而,他们需要专门知识才能很好地执行,甚至对熟练的编辑来说也依然乏味(Dmytryk等,2018年)。
在这部作品中,我们通过开发新的互动工具来应对这些挑战,使微版更易于探索和应用,并侧重于对话场景,这在叙事片中尤为常见(Cutting, 2021). 我们的工作包括四个部分:

blocks.en: • First, we examine how and why expert filmmakers use micro-edits through a formative user study, detailed in Section 3 . We found that experts use micro-edits in two distinct ways: to manipulate the timing of a narrative (rhythm edits), and to direct visual attention (view edits). • Next, we formalize the space of possible micro-edits for a given scene in Section 4 , and use our formulation to describe different editing constraints and objectives. This allows us to address micro-editing as an optimization problem and incorporate analyses provided by vision-language models (VLMs), when available. • Then, building on our formalization, we design novel interactive tools that leverage optimization and AI to efficiently explore micro-edits through interactions that map more clearly and consistently to common creative goals. • Finally, we validate our tools in Section 6 through a crowdsourced study and two evaluations with 16 experienced editors, showing that they reduce mechanical effort and support broader exploration of micro-edits.

blocks.en: Our work combines user-centered design with the development of novel technical tools. The design contributions in our work deal with understanding how micro-edits are used so we can build better editing tools, while our technical contributions address challenges that emerge when applying computation to that understanding. Our formative findings translate into two design goals: efficient exploration and useful suggestions (Section 3.5 ). We use these goals to motivate and evaluate our tools.

blocks.en: 2. Related Work
blocks.zh: 2. 相关工作

blocks.en: While our work is, to our knowledge, the first to address interactive tools for micro-editing, prior work in vision, graphics, and HCI has looked at related problems, including rough cut assembly.
blocks.zh: 虽然据我们所知,我们的工作是首先处理用于微观编辑的交互式工具,但先前在视觉、图形和HCI方面的工作都研究了相关问题,包括粗剪组装。

blocks.en: 2.1. Macro-Level Editing and Assembly
blocks.zh: 2.1. 宏观一级的编辑和大会

blocks.en: Computational tools for video editing primarily target content selection and rough-cut assembly. Systems for scripted dialogue encode cinematographic idioms to decide which clips appear and in what order ( Leake et al., 2017 ; Leake and Li, 2024 ) . Transcript-based interfaces ( Truong et al., 2016 ; Casares et al., 2002 ; Pavel et al., 2015 ) enable text-driven manipulation, while keyword analysis recommends B-roll insertion points ( Huber et al., 2019 ) . More recent LLM-powered systems infer editorial intent from natural language ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , combine language with sketch-based control ( Tilekbay et al., 2024 ) , and support human–AI co-creation for generating rough-cuts ( Sandoval-Castaneda et al., 2025 ; Huh et al., 2025 ) . Recent work on automated montage assembly learns shot selection, trimming, and cut placement from professionally edited films, but does not provide explicit editor control over micro-edits, including decoupled audio and video transitions ( Sandoval-Castañeda et al., 2026 ) . These systems operate at word- or shot-level granularity, which is effective for structuring a scene, but they stop short of the frame-level refinement where professional editors shape timing and attention.
blocks.zh: 视频编辑的计算工具主要针对内容选择和粗剪组装. 用于脚本对话框的系统编码为电影平面,以决定哪些片段出现以及顺序(Leake等,2017;Leake和Li,2024.). 基于语录的界面 (Truong等,2016;Casares等,2002;Pavel等,2015)允许由文本驱动的操作,而关键词分析则推荐B-roll插入点(Huber等,2019). 较近期的LLM动力系统推断出自然语言的编辑意图(Wang等,2024年),将语言与草图控制相结合(Tilekbay等,2024年),并支持人类-AI共创生成粗剪图(Sandoval-Castaneda等,2025年;Huh等,2025年). 近期关于自动蒙太热组装的工作从专业编辑的电影中学习了镜头选择,剪接,并剪接了投放,但并未对微编辑提供明确的编辑控制,包括解接的音频和视频过渡(Sandoval-Castañeda等,2026年). 这些系统在文字或相片级的颗粒性上运作,这对构建一个场景是有效的,但它们在专业编辑塑造出时机和注意力的帧级完善中止步.

blocks.en: 2.2. Automated Cut Placement and Pacing
blocks.zh: 2.2. 自动剪接和安放

blocks.en: Commercial tools provide filler-word removal and silence compression to streamline rough cuts ( Descript, 2025 ; OpusClip, 2025 ; CapCut, 2025 ) . Adobe Premiere plugins like AutoCut ( 2025 ) and FireCut ( 2025 ) extend this by offering configurable offsets within silence-removal workflows, where audio is cut earlier than video by a fixed amount to smooth transitions (split edits). These workflows treat pacing as uniform temporal compression and treat split edits as mechanical timing offsets. Such behavior is well-suited to high-volume social and podcast workflows with strict duration constraints and tolerance for jump-cut rhythm, but misaligned with dramatic editing where silence is expressive and overlap is applied selectively to anticipate or extend specific beats. Our work formalizes these micro-editing operations and introduces an interactive tool for selective, frame-level refinement of rhythm and visual emphasis after rough-cut assembly. Rather than applying uniform pacing or fixed offsets, our system surfaces alternatives and perceptual cues tied to narrative beats and viewer attention.
blocks.zh: 商业工具提供填字去除和静音压缩以精简粗略的剪接(描述,2025;OpusClip,2025;CapCut,2025.). Adobe Primee插件如AutoCut (2025)和FireCut (2025) 扩展此功能,在消音工作流程中提供可配置的抵消,其中音频比视频提前被固定数量剪切到平稳过渡(分集编辑). 这些工作流程将间距作为统一的时间压缩处理,将分化编辑作为机械计时抵消处理. 这种行为非常适合高容量的社会和播客工作流程,对跳跃节奏有严格的持续时间限制和耐受性,但与戏剧性编辑错配,其中沉默是表现性的并有选择地应用重叠来预测或延伸特定的节拍. 我们的工作使这些微编辑操作正规化,并引入了一个互动工具,用于在粗剪后对节奏和视觉强调进行选择性、帧级的改进。 我们的系统不采用统一的节奏或固定的相抵方式,而是呈现与叙事节拍和观众注意力相联的替代和感知提示。

blocks.en: The closest prior work at comparable granularity is Berthouzoz et al. (2012) , who analyze audio-visual features in single-speaker interview footage to locate frames where the subject is quiet and still, enabling hidden transitions via graph-based frame selection. Our work differs in three respects: (1) we address multi-clip dialogue with multiple speakers and camera angles; (2) we support audio–video decoupling through split edits rather than solely audio-aligned straight cuts; and (3) we provide interactive exploration of alternatives rather than optimizing for a single global solution.
blocks.zh: 前作中最接近可比较颗粒度的作品是Berthouzoz等人(2012年),他在单声道采访镜头中分析视听特征,以定位被试对象静静而静静的帧,通过图框选择实现隐藏的过渡. 我们的工作在三个方面有所不同:(1) 我们用多种发言者和相机角度进行多剪接对话;(2) 我们支持通过分版编辑而不是仅仅通过音频对接直截了当的剪接来进行音频-视频脱钩;(3) 我们为单一全球解决方案提供互动探索,而不是优化。

blocks.en: 2.3. Micro-Temporal Signals for Editing
blocks.zh: 2.3. 用于编辑的微时信号

blocks.en: Editors time cuts to perceptual events that guide attention and maintain continuity ( Smith, 2012 ; Smith and Mital, 2013 ) . Conventions such as cutting mid-action ( Dmytryk et al., 2018 ) , decoupling picture and sound cut points, and avoiding cuts on blinks exploit motion continuity, dialogue structure, and audio-visual synchrony ( Murch, 2025 ; Salt, 2011 ) . Galvane et al. (2015) encode some continuity constraints over screen position, gaze, and motion, and optimize shot sequences accordingly in virtual environments where scene state is available. In practice, these constraints often compete, and their relative importance depends on narrative context.

blocks.en: In real footage, these cues can be inferred from audio-visual signals, including gaze and blink via facial landmark tracking ( Lugaresi et al., 2019 ) and audio-visual synchrony ( Owens and Efros, 2018 ; Sun et al., 2023 ) . Prior work aligns or matches video using appearance similarity ( Wang et al., 2014 ) , motion trajectories or optical flow for action synchronization ( Arev et al., 2014 ; Bazin and Sorkine-Hornung, 2016 ; Chen et al., 2023 ) , and learned features for continuity scoring and transition classification ( Pardo et al., 2021 ; Pardo et al., 2022 ) .
blocks.zh: 在真实的镜头中,这些提示可以从视听信号中推断出,包括通过面部地标跟踪(Lugaresi等,2019年)和视听同步(Owens和Efros,2018年;Sun等,2023年)进行凝视和眨眼. 先前的工作利用外观相似性(Wang等,2014年),运动轨迹或光学流来配合动作同步(Arev等,2014年;Bazin和Sorkine-Hornung,2016年;Chen等,2023年),以及连续性评分和过渡分类的学习特征(Pardo等,2021年;Pardo等,2022年).

blocks.en: Semantics can further indicate which alignments are editorially salient. Recent VLMs, when supplied with numbered-frame inputs ( Wu et al., 2025 ) and short, densely sampled clips ( Qu et al., 2025 ) , can identify such moments (e.g., a door slam, a character’s turn). We build on these semantic and audio-visual cues to surface micro-edit opportunities within an interactive workflow.
blocks.zh: 语义学可以进一步说明哪些对齐在编辑上是突出的. 近期的VLM,当提供编号框输入(Wu等,2025年)和短而密集的采样片段(Qu等,2025年)时,可以识别出这样的瞬间(例如:一扇门被撞倒,一个人物的转弯). 我们利用这些语义和视听提示,在互动工作流程中展示微观编辑机会。

blocks.en: 3. Background and Formative Study
blocks.zh: 3个 背景和格式研究

blocks.en: We conducted a formative study with six experienced editors (5–15 years experience) to understand how and why they adjust rough cuts. Full details of our study are included as supplemental material, and we summarize our findings below.
blocks.zh: 我们与六位经验丰富的编辑(5至15年的经验)进行了成形研究,以了解他们如何以及为什么调整粗略削减。 我们的研究的全部细节作为补充材料列入,我们总结如下。

blocks.en: 3.1. Background
blocks.zh: 3.1. 背景情况

blocks.en:
Our study design incorporates additional background related to how editors often discuss cuts , which represent transitions on a timeline (video, audio, or both) from one piece of source media to another.
Note that the term “cut” has two meanings in editing: it can refer to a transition point between clips, or to a version of the edit (as in “rough cut” or “final cut”). Here we discuss cuts as transition points.
Editors classify most cuts into one of three categories: • Straight cuts happen when video and audio transition together. • L-cuts happen when video transitions before audio. • J-cuts happen when audio transitions before video. Additionally, the term “split cut” is sometimes used to describe any cut that is not a straight cut. Implicit in these categories is an assumption that both audio and video transition between corresponding source media. While not always true, this describes most cuts found outside specific genres like music videos.
blocks.zh:
我们的研究设计包含了更多与编辑们如何经常讨论剪接相关的背景,
请注意,“剪接”一词在编辑中有两个含义:它可以指片段之间的一个过渡点,也可以指编辑的版本(如"rough cut"或"final cut"). 在这里,我们讨论削减作为过渡点。
编辑将大多数切口归为三类之一: • 视频和音频过渡时发生直切. • 视频在音频之前转换时发生L剪接。 • J-剪接发生在视频之前的音频转换。 此外,有时还用 " 剪接 " 一词来形容任何不是直截的剪接。 这些类别中隐含着一种假设,即相应的源媒体之间的音频和视频过渡. 虽然并不总是真实的,但这描述了在音乐视频等特定流派之外发现的大多数切口.

blocks.en: Straight cuts happen when video and audio transition together.
blocks.zh: 当视频和音频转换在一起时,就会发生直切.

blocks.en: L-cuts happen when video transitions before audio.
blocks.zh: L-剪接发生在音频前的视频转换.

blocks.en: J-cuts happen when audio transitions before video.
blocks.zh: J-剪接发生在视频之前的音频转换.

blocks.en: Macro-editing is often limited to straight cuts, and previous computational tools have made this an explicit assumption when formulating rough cut assembly ( Leake et al., 2017 ; Truong et al., 2016 ; Huh et al., 2025 ) . This points to L- and J-cuts as offering some insight into how editors think about micro-editing, which we leverage in our formative study design.
blocks.zh: 宏观编辑往往仅限于直截了当的剪接,之前的计算工具在制定粗剪接组装时将此作为明确的假设(Leake等,2017;Truong等,2016;Huh等,2025.). 这指向L-和J-cuts提供了一些对编辑们如何思考微编辑的洞察力,我们利用微编辑在我们的成形研究设计中.

blocks.en: 3.2. Study Design
blocks.zh: 3.2. 研究设计

blocks.en: Each participant was given rough cuts of two scripted scenes (each approximately one-minute long) and tasked with editing each scene in an NLE of their choice under four conditions. In one condition, participants were unrestricted. For each of the remaining three conditions, we asked participants to limit edits to different cut types: straight cuts, L-cuts, or J-cuts. Participants were recorded and asked to explain their reasoning aloud while editing, and after completing their tasks, each participant filled out a survey.
blocks.zh: 每个参与者都被粗略地剪取了两个脚本场景(每个场景约1分钟长),并负责在4个条件下按照自己选择的NLE编辑每个场景. 在一个条件下,与会者不受限制。 对于其余三个条件,我们要求参与者将编辑限制在不同的剪接类型:直切,L剪接,或J剪接. 记录了与会者,并要求他们在编辑时大声解释其推理,在完成任务后,每位与会者填写一份调查。

blocks.en: 3.3. Formative Findings
blocks.zh: 3.3. 格式调查结果

blocks.en: F1 ) Every Frame Matters: Our study reinforced the common claim that skilled editors often make decisions at the scale of individual frames ( Murch, 2001 ; Dmytryk et al., 2018 ) . While making micro-edits, participants described “ going frame by frame, removing one frame here, adding a few there ” (P5) or “ adding 3 or 4 more frames ” (P1) to get transitions to feel just right. This process also involved repeatedly re-watching parts of video to compare the feel of different choices.
blocks.zh: F1) 每个框架事项: 我们的研究强化了共同的主张,即熟练的编辑常常按照单个帧的规模作出决定(Murch,2001;Dmytryk等,2018年)。 在制作微观编辑时,与会者描述了“逐个框架进行,删除一个框架,在这里增加几个框架......”(P5)或“增加3或4个框架......”(P1),以使过渡变得正确。 这一过程还涉及反复重看部分视频来比较不同选择的感觉.

blocks.en: F2 ) Contextual Information is Important: Editing decisions often depend on local context. For example, editors generally place audio cuts in silent parts of a clip. On the other hand, they often adjust visual cuts based on narrative goals (e.g., cutting to see a particular character’s reaction during a dramatic moment), or following the “cut on action” principle ( Dmytryk et al., 2018 ; Chandler, 2012 ) , where visuals before and after a cut should show the continuity of some visible action (e.g., a gesture, blink, or gaze turn). This type of higher-level reasoning helps editors narrow their choice of edit.
blocks.zh: F2) 上下文信息很重要:编辑决定往往取决于本地背景. 例如,编辑一般会将音频剪接放入剪辑中无声的部分. 另一方面,他们经常根据叙事目标来调整视觉剪接(例如剪接以在剧情中看到特定角色的反应),或者遵循"剪接动作"原则(Dmytryk等,2018;Chandler,2012),剪接前后的视觉应该显示出一些可见动作的连续性(例如手势,眨眼,或凝视转弯等). 这种更高级的推理有助于编辑者缩小对编辑的选择.

blocks.en:
F3 ) Control Over Rhythm & Pacing: Editors often start with edits meant to control the precise rhythm or pacing of a scene—usually by inserting or removing time at the ends of adjacent clips. We call this type of adjustment a rhythm edit . Rhythm edits change how events are distributed on the timeline; for example, in dialogue-heavy scenes, they can be used to control the length of pauses in conversation. Half of our participants described focusing exclusively on the timing of dialogue while making such edits, with one (P6) describing this process as starting with a “ radio edit ”, and another (P4) saying “ I’m going to close my eyes and listen … this lets me really focus on the flow and not be interrupted by some video breaks. ”
Rhythm edits require shifting a clip along the output timeline, often in addition to adjusting the duration of a clip.
blocks.zh:
F3) Control Over Rhythm & Pacing:编辑器经常以编辑为起点,意在控制一个场景的精确节奏或节奏——通常是在相邻剪接片尾插入或去除时间. 我们称这种调整为节奏编辑。 韵律编辑会改变事件在时间线上的分布方式;例如,在对话重的场景中,可以用来控制对话中暂停的长度. 我们一半的与会者说,在进行这种编辑时,只注重对话的时间,有一个(P6)说,这一进程始于“电台编辑”,另一个(P4)说,“我要闭上眼睛,倾听............”。 这让我真正专注于流动,而不是被一些视频中断打断。 “
韵律编辑需要沿着输出时间线来移动一个剪辑,往往除了调整剪辑的时间外.

blocks.en: F4 ) Control Over Visual Attention: Later edits often focus on controlling visual attention. We can think of these edits, which we call view edits , as controlling the viewpoint of the audience without changing the timeline of events that are happening. View edits are where participants tended to make L-cuts and J-cuts. More specifically, L-cuts were mostly used to make visual transitions happen sooner, while J-cuts were used to make them happen later. In both cases, this was usually done without changing the audio track. To quote one participant (P1), “ I already changed the timing of the audio… so I don’t wanna, like, mess with that. ”
blocks.zh: F4) Control Over Visual Ention:后期编辑时常注重于控制视觉注意力. 我们可以把这些编辑(我们称之为取景编辑)视为控制观众观点,而不改变正在发生的事件的时间安排。 视图编辑是参与者倾向于制作L剪接和J剪接的地方. 更具体地说,L-cuts大多被用来让视觉过渡更早地实现,而J-cuts则被用来让它们更晚地实现. 在这两种情况下,这通常都是在不改变音轨的情况下完成的. 引用一位与会者(P1)的话,“我已经改变了录音的时间......。 所以我不想, “

blocks.en: F5 ) Inserting New Cuts For Reactions & Cutaways: In our study, most edits involved adjusting existing cuts. The main exception to this happened when editors wanted to add a reaction or cutaway shot, where visuals transition away from the speaker or current source of audio. Two reasons were given for such edits: first, to direct visual attention; and second, to mask jump cuts (created when trimming pauses within dialogue). Also, editors often repurpose visuals from other parts of a scene to create reaction shots. This points to conditions where reordering clips in a scene is acceptable.
blocks.zh: F5) 插入新的响应剪接和剪接: 在我们的研究中,大多数编辑涉及调整现有的削减。 主要例外发生在编辑想添加反应或剪接镜头时,视觉从扬声器或当前音频来源过渡出. 这种编辑有两个原因:第一,引导视觉注意力;第二,遮住跳跃剪接(在对话框中进行裁剪时创建). 另外,编辑经常从场景的其他部分重用视觉来产生反应镜头. 这说明一个场景的重排片段是可以接受的条件.

blocks.en: 3.4. Design Insights
blocks.zh: 3.4. 设计透视

blocks.en: F1 and F2 reflect that micro-editing does not have a unique solution, and precise user control is important, though evaluating contextual and semantic information may help automate some decisions.
blocks.zh: F1和F2反映了微编辑没有独特的解决方案,准确的用户控制很重要,尽管评价上下文和语义信息可能有助于一些决定自动化.

blocks.en: F3 and F4 suggest that editors treat rhythm and views separately; thus, controls for these aspects should be independent. This separation reflects how editors exploit audio-visual synchrony , as one participant (P1) articulated: “ What you hear and what you see are two different systems… if you introduce the hearing as one sense and then introduce the sight, it’s a different feeling than if you introduce both at the same time. ” Our tools are designed to help users focus on each type of control separately. F5 suggests that showing only speakers means audiences miss half of the story—character reactions—so editors spend significant time scrubbing through takes to find them. A tool that surfaces candidates would help.
blocks.zh: F3和F4建议编辑分别处理节奏和观点;因此,对这些方面的控制应该是独立的. 正如一位与会者(P1)所阐明的那样,这种分离反映了编辑如何利用视听同步性:“你听到的和看到的是两个不同的系统......。 如果你将听觉作为一种感官引入,然后将视觉引入,这与同时将两者引入的感觉不同。 我们的工具旨在帮助用户分别关注每一种类型的控制. F5表示,只显示演讲者意味着观众错过了一半的故事——特征反应——所以编辑们花费了相当长的时间,通过各种途径寻找他们。 一个让候选人露面的工具会有所帮助。

blocks.en: 3.5. Design Goals
blocks.zh: 3.5. 设计目标

blocks.en: Different micro-edits may accomplish different creative goals, which can be highly context-dependent. This lack of a single correct solution complicates automation, but there is still a great deal that optimization and AI can offer to improve existing workflows. Micro-edits are not random, and the space of all possible edits is much larger than the set that meet likely creative goals. With this in mind, we focus on two overarching design goals in this work:
blocks.zh: 不同的微观编辑可能实现不同的创造性目标,而这些目标可能高度依赖上下文。 这种缺乏单一的正确解决方案使自动化复杂化了,但目前仍有大量优化和AI可以提供改进现有工作流程. 微编辑不是随机的,所有可能的编辑的空间都比达到可能创造性目标的集要大得多. 考虑到这一点,我们侧重于这项工作的两个总体设计目标:

blocks.en: DG1 ) More Efficient Exploration: Our findings ( F1 ) illustrate that much of the challenge in making micro-edits comes from a “gulf of execution” ( Norman, 2002 ) between changes users want to make and the steps those changes require in existing non-linear editors (NLEs). Our tools should make micro-edits easier to execute when possible, letting users explore the same edit space more efficiently.
blocks.zh: DG1) 更高效地探索: 我们的研究结果(F1)表明,制作微型编辑的很多挑战来自用户希望作出的改动与现有非线性编辑器(NLEs)中这些改动要求采取的步骤之间的“执行之盾”(Norman, 2002年)。 我们的工具应该使微编辑在可能时更容易执行,让用户更有效地探索同样的编辑空间.

blocks.en: DG2 ) Useful Defaults & Suggestions: As we discuss in Section 4 , this space is continuous, but editors often reason about micro-edits in ways that give rise to more discrete sets of likely editing decisions. Our tool should help identify such decisions and present them to users as defaults or suggestions.
blocks.zh: DG2) 有用的默认和建议( O) : 但编辑们往往会以更分散的方式解释微编辑的决定。 我们的工具应帮助确定此类决定,并作为缺省或建议提交用户。

blocks.en: These design goals reflect a need to balance automation with expressive control: our findings identify the types of control that editors want, and our tools focus on automating the work that makes this control less efficient. Meeting these goals requires describing this space precisely, which we do in the next section.
blocks.zh: 这些设计目标反映出需要平衡自动化和表达控制:我们的结论确定了编辑想要的控制类型,我们的工具侧重于使这种控制效率降低的工作自动化. 要实现这些目标,就需要准确描述这一空间,我们在下一节中这样做。

blocks.en: 4. Problem Formulation
blocks.zh: 4. 问题的提出

blocks.en:
We describe editing as a two-stage process, starting with macro-edits, followed by micro-edits. We use this framing to distinguish two types of editing decisions, not to claim that editing proceeds strictly in this order in practice. The input to this process is a set of source media and optional narrative description. Source media is given as a set 𝐌 = { M , ∅ M , 1 … } \mathbf{M{}}{}=\{M{}_{\varnothing},M{}_{1},...\} of clips, where M ∅ M{}_{\varnothing} represents the empty clip (i.e., what is displayed if part of a timeline is left empty).
The narrative, if provided (e.g., in the form of a script or storyboard), is represented with a sequence of narrative elements 𝐒 = [ s 1 , s 2 , … ] \mathbf{S}{}=[s_{1},s_{2},...] , where each s i s_{i} describes a different part of the narrative. We use s i ⊂ M j s_{i}\subset M{}_{j} to indicate that s i s_{i} is portrayed in source media M j M{}_{j} , and M ( s i ) j M{}_{j}(s_{i}) to denote the part of M j M{}_{j} that depicts s i s_{i} . We leave the definition of narrative elements [ s 1 , s 2 , … ] [s_{1},s_{2},...] intentionally loose, as their primary role is to segment source media and express partial orderings during macro-editing. We will introduce more precise notation later for discussing narrative events in micro-edits.

blocks.en: 4.1. Rough Cuts & Macro-Editing
blocks.zh: 4.1. 粗剪和宏观编辑

blocks.en:
The goal of macro-editing is to produce a rough cut 𝐑 \mathbf{R}{} , given as an ordered sequence of source clips. blocks.en: 4.3. Micro-Editing Constraints & Context
blocks.zh: 4.3. 微观编辑制约因素和背景

blocks.en: We identify two types of constraints that impact micro-editing: • Synchrony constraints ensure that visible sound sources are heard (e.g., we hear a character who is visibly speaking). This constraint is one-directional: hearing off-screen sound is acceptable, which enables L- and J-cuts. We quantify this via synchrony ( Dixon and Spitz, 1980 ; Roseboom et al., 2009 ; Vatakis and Spence, 2006 ) : audio and video should stay coupled in high-synchrony regions. • Continuity constraints maintain consistency across cuts. For example, when cutting to different viewpoints of the same scene, the poses and appearance of characters should remain largely unchanged. Similarly, when cutting to different audio of the same scene, one should avoid cutting in the middle of salient sound, as this can create audible discontinuities. Both of these types deal with some types of consistency: between audio and video, or across cuts. Strictly speaking, there are no editing patterns that these constraints prevent in all scenarios; each depends on the context of a particular scene. To help reason about this, we need a way to represent context in source media. Unlike the coarse narrative elements 𝐒 \mathbf{S}{} used for macro-editing, micro-editing requires fine-grained events—blinks, action onsets, reactions, word boundaries. We denote these 𝐄 = [ e 1 , e 2 , … ] \mathbf{E}{}=[e_{1},e_{2},...] , with M ( e i ) j M{}_{j}(e_{i}) denoting the time in M j M{}_{j} where e i e_{i} occurs. The key context function is synchrony σ ( M , j t ) \sigma{}(M{}_{j},t) , representing audio-visual alignment at time t t . The next section describes how our system uses these constraints and context to support micro-editing tools.

blocks.en: 5.2. Rhythm Edits

blocks.en:
Rhythm edits adjust cut timing while maintaining track coupling ( V i = A i V_{i}=A_{i} ). Repositioning a cut changes both x o ​ u ​ t i x^{i}_{out} and x i ​ n i x^{i}_{in} , pulling dialogue earlier (time-contracting) or pushing it later (time-expanding) without cutting into speech. As noted in F3 , editors often focus on temporal flow when adjusting rhythm, yet existing NLEs require spatial manipulation of timeline elements. To address this, we provide two hotkey interactions: (1) pre-roll hotkey rewinds before the current cut to provide conversational context. (2) A trim/extend hotkey repositions the cut so that the first word of the incoming clip (following X i + 1 X_{i+1} ) lands at the current playhead position p p . If p < x i + 1 o ​ u ​ t p<\text{x}{}^{i+1}_{out} , the system advances the cut (time-contracting, closing the silence gap).
If p > x i + 1 o ​ u ​ t p>\text{x}{}^{i+1}_{out} , the system delays the cut (time-expanding, revealing silence).
This enables marking timing by feel : Murch (2001) describes marking a shot’s cut point in real time and treating his ability to consistently “hit the same frame” as confirmation that the timing is right, adjusting until he can ( Murch, 2025 ) .

Cut-on-Action: This mode surfaces candidates where motion continues smoothly across the cut (Figure 3 D). Since VLMs struggle with micro-temporal reasoning ( Qu et al., 2025 ) , we densely sample frames from the handles (outgoing post-roll and incoming pre-roll) and assemble them into numbered mosaics (Figure 6 ). Explicit frame indices improve temporal grounding ( Wu et al., 2025 ) .
The VLM identifies frame pairs with salient motion continuity (e.g., matching gesture trajectory, gaze direction), and indices are converted to offsets δ i \delta_{i} within W v W{}_{\text{v}}{} . Restricting candidates to W v W{}_{\text{v}}{} means the VLM reasons over a few synchrony-safe frames rather than the full footage.

blocks.zh: 5.4. 反应射击

blocks.en: Unlike rhythm and view edits, which adjust existing cuts, reaction shots add new visual material on an overlay track (B-roll) without altering the primary audio timeline ( F5 ). We identify candidate segments where σ ( M , j t ) = 0 \sigma{}(M{}_{j},t)=0 (subject visible but not speaking), the target subject is detected in at least 80% of frames, and the segment is adjacent to spoken material. To support browsing, candidates are indexed by subject identity and emotion using EmoCLIP ( Foteinopoulou and Patras, 2024 ) . The interface groups results by character and emotion (Figure 3 A). This supports both expressive goals (showing a character’s reaction) and practical needs (masking jump cuts from rhythm tightening).

blocks.en: 5.5. Implementation
blocks.zh: 5.5. 执行情况

blocks.en:
We implemented MicroEditor as a web-based editor forked from ClipJS ( Mohyware, 2024 ) , extending it with multi-track timeline support, rolling edits, and the tools described above.
An offline pipeline preprocesses each source clip to extract word-level timestamps (via ASR ( Radford et al., 2023 ) ), per-frame synchrony scores, and subject identity. For synchrony, we use active speaker detection ( Liao et al., 2025 ) for dialogue scenes and an audio-visual alignment network ( Morgado et al., 2021 ) for non-dialogue content. We threshold the continuous signal to obtain σ ( M , j t ) ∈ { 0 , 1 } \sigma{}(M{}_{j},t)\in\{0,1\} , where σ = 1 \sigma{}=1 indicates salient audio-visual alignment (e.g., an on-screen face visibly speaking in dialogue scenes) and σ = 0 \sigma{}=0 otherwise (Figure 5 ); see Appendix B for VLM prompts and more details.
All VLM queries use Gemini 3.0 Flash. VLMs are used to annotate source clips during preprocessing (e.g., subject identity and shot type) and to search for cut-on-action candidates, where our formalization bounds the search to the editing window W v W{}_{\text{v}}{} (Section 5.3 ).

blocks.en: 6. Evaluation
blocks.zh: 6. 国家 评价

blocks.en: We first validated our synchrony analysis through a crowdsourced study, and then evaluated MicroEditor in two comparative studies with experienced editors, focusing on our design goals: whether our tools enable more efficient exploration of the micro-edit space ( DG1 ), and whether our defaults and suggestions help editors identify desirable edits ( DG2 ). Study 1 (N = 6) evaluated the initial system and validated tools for rhythm and view editing. Based on feedback, we refined the interface and added a Reaction Shot Browser. Study 2 (N = 10) evaluated this expanded system with an additional focus on reaction shot selection and perceived improvements in scene pacing and visual flow. Because micro-editing has no single correct solution and desirable edits depend on creative goals (Section 3.5 ), our evaluation emphasizes workflow support, decision support, and exploration rather than correctness against a fixed ground truth. Full study protocols and other evaluation details can be found in our supplemental materials.
blocks.zh: 我们首先通过多方联动的研究验证了我们的同步分析,然后在与经验丰富的编辑器的两次比较研究中评价了MicroEditor,侧重于我们的设计目标:我们的工具是否能够更有效地探索微编辑器空间(DG1),以及我们的默认和建议是否帮助编辑器识别理想的编辑器(DG2). 第1研究(N=6)评价了初始系统并验证了节奏和取景编辑的工具. 根据反馈,我们完善了界面,并增加了一个反应相片浏览器. 研究2(N = 10)评价了这个被扩展的系统,并额外侧重于反应镜头选择和场景速度和视觉流感的改善. 由于微编辑没有单一的正确解决方案,理想的编辑取决于创意目标(第3.5节),因此我们的评价强调工作流程支持,决策支持和探索,而不是针对固定的地盘真理的正确性. 完整的研究规程和其他评价细节见我们的补充材料。

blocks.en:
To validate our method for decoupling audio and video, we conducted a Prolific study ( N = 47 N=47 ; 4 excluded for failing attention checks). Participants viewed 12 randomized clips ( ∼ 5 {\sim}5 s each) across three conditions: Optimized (cut inside W W{} ), Boundary (cut on the window edge), and Out-of-Window (fixed offset outside the window). For each clip, participants reported whether they noticed any distracting lip-sync errors or AV mismatches and rated how natural or smooth the cut felt on a 7-point scale (1 = very jarring, 7 = very smooth). Results show a significant main effect of condition on naturalness ( p < .001 p<.001 , Friedman test). Post-hoc tests confirmed Optimized cuts were rated significantly more natural than both Boundary ( p = .001 p=.001 ) and Out-of-Window ( p < .001 p<.001 ) conditions. In aggregate, Optimized clips achieved the lowest violation rate (32.4%) and highest naturalness ( M = 5.27 M=5.27 ), vs. Out-of-Window (85.1%, M = 3.10 M=3.10 ) (Figure 7 ).
Notably, excluding the Soup Spoon scene where upstream face-tracking errors produced an unreliable synchrony window, the Optimized violation rate drops to 19.9% ( M = 5.67 M=5.67 ). We note that our method’s performance is inherently bounded by the capabilities of the underlying AV-sync model.
blocks.zh:
为了验证我们的音频和视频脱钩方法,我们进行了一次Prolific研究(N = 47 N = 47;4因注意检查失败而排除)。 与会者浏览了12个随机剪辑(每次5 s): 优化(切入W WQQ),边界(切入出窗边缘),出窗(固定相抵出窗外). 对于每个片段,参与者都报告说他们是否注意到了任何分心的唇音同步错误或AV不匹配,并评分了切口在7分尺度(1=非常活泼,7=非常平滑)上的自然感或平滑感. 结果显示,病情对自然具有重大的主要影响(第001页,第001页,弗里德曼试验)。 经证实的艾滋病毒后检测 与边界(p=.001 p=.001)和出窗(p <.001 p < 001)条件相比,优化的削减被评为明显地更自然。 总而言之,优化片段实现了最低的违规率(32.4%)和最高的自然(M=5.27 M=5.27),对出窗(85.1%,M=3.10 M=3.10)(图7).
值得注意的是,不包括上游面孔跟踪错误产生不可靠同步窗口的Soup Spoon场景,优化违规率降至19.9%(M=5.67 M=5.67)。 我们注意到,我们的方法的性能从本质上看取决于基本的AV同步模型的能力。

blocks.en: 6.2. User Studies
blocks.zh: 6.2. 用户研究

blocks.en:
We recruited 6 professional video editors for Study 1 (3 female, 3 male, aged 18–27) with 5–15 years of experience, all primarily using Adobe Premiere Pro, and 10 video editors for Study 2 (6 female, 4 male, aged 19–28, 1–10 years of experience) working across narrative films, commercial content, documentaries, and YouTube. Both studies followed the same protocol: each participant edited two one-minute dialogue scenes (“Pumpkin Princess” and “Anesthesia”) under a manual condition (all features disabled) and an assisted condition (all features enabled), in counterbalanced order.
Sessions lasted 60 minutes.
Participants rated feature usefulness and creativity support on 7-point Likert scales (Table 1 ).
Study 2 additionally collected ratings on pacing and visual flow, and logged all interactions with millisecond timestamps; one participant’s (P9) log was not recorded due to a logging error, so quantitative analyses cover the remaining nine participants ( N = 9 N=9 ).
Full demographics and per-participant ratings appear in Appendices C and D ; participant IDs below refer to each study separately.
blocks.zh:
我们为第一研究招聘了6名专业录像编辑(3名女性、3名男性、18-27岁),他们拥有5-15年的经验,他们主要使用Adobe Primee Pro,为第二研究招聘了10名录像编辑(6名女性、4名男性、19-28岁、1-10年的经验),从事叙事电影、商业内容、纪录片和YouTube。 这两项研究都遵循同一规程:每位参与者都以手动条件(所有功能均被禁用)和辅助条件(所有功能均被启用)为顺序,编辑了两场一分钟的对话场景(“南瓜公主”和“爱思奇艺”)。
会议持续了60分钟。
参与者在7分的Irikrt比例表(表1)上评为实用性和创造性支持。
研究2另外收集了对相距和视流的评分,并记录了所有与毫秒印记的相互作用;一名参与者的(P9)日志由于伐木错误而未被记录,因此定量分析覆盖了其余9名参与者(N=9 N=9).
完整的人口统计和每个参与者的评级载于附录C和D;下文的参与者身份证分别提及每项研究。

blocks.en:
Rhythm Editing: In Study 1, editors found the pre-roll and trim/extend hotkeys useful (median 6.0/7) and efficient (median 7.0/7; DG1 ).
Pre-roll enabled the repeated listening behavior essential for rhythm editing ( F3 ).
P3 emphasized repetition: “ As an editor I like to hear and see the cut at least 10 times and it was easy to replay it using the pre-roll key. ”
P6 articulated why context matters: “ I think the R [pre-roll] feature is something that I really like to just quickly go back… you kind of have to get a little bit of context further, just to get into the flow of that, and then you can watch the cut again. ”
blocks.zh:
韵律编辑:在"一号研究"中,编辑们发现预卷和trim/extend热键有用(中间6.0/7)并高效(中间7.0/7;DG1.
Pre-roll 启用了对节奏编辑至关重要的重复收听行为(F3 ).
P3强调重复:“作为一名编辑,我至少希望听到和看到10次剪辑,使用预卷键很容易重放。 “
P6阐述了背景为何重要:“我认为,R[前卷]的特征正是我真正喜欢的,只是迅速回到...... 你必须要有 一点点上下文, 只是进入流动, 然后你可以再次观看切。 “

blocks.en:
Character Focus: Participants valued the automated L/J cuts as a starting point that offloaded mechanical work for creative decisions.
P3 appreciated the cognitive offloading: “ You always know in a scene which character is the main one… it was nice to get [character focus] done straight away so I can focus on other things. ”
P2 said: “ I used one pass to emphasize speaker and was blown away with how accurately it created the space for the character. ”
P1 confirmed: “ There weren’t many specific edits I needed to keep making based off of those automatic cuts, and those cuts would have taken a while manually. ”
Character Focus was rated 7.0/7 (median), validating F4 and DG2 .
In Study 2, P3 similarly noted that the automated cuts “ tended to feel natural and would be similar to what I would do as an editor without these tools .”
blocks.zh:
角色焦点:参与者重视自动L/J剪接作为卸载机械工作的起点,用于创造性决策.
P3欣赏了认知卸载:"你总是在某一场景中知道哪个角色是主角...... 我很高兴能马上完成这个工作 这样我就能专注于其他事情 “
P2说:“我用一个通行证来强调演讲者,被吹走,因为它为这个角色创造了多么准确的空间。 “
P1证实:"我不需要多少具体的编辑, “
字符焦点被评为7.0/7 (中间),验证F4和DG2 .
在研究2中,P3同样指出,自动化剪接“往往感觉很自然,而且与没有这些工具我作为编辑的工作类似”。

blocks.en:
Cut-on-Action: Cut-on-Action markers (median 7.0/7) transformed the tedious frame-level search into discrete choices ( F2 ).
P5 noted: “ Cut on Action suggestions took the painstaking process of having to find each moment of large action and match it with another clip and made it extremely simple, with very strong accuracy. ”
P1 described the reduction in decision fatigue: “ Just having the markers to choose from helped prevent decision fatigue. When you have so many frames versus just the three options, it helps you narrow it down. ”
In Study 2, P4 described using markers for narrative construction: “ I used this feature to help inform my overall approach to the video narrative for each scene. If there was a particular narrative goal I wanted to achieve, I used the Cut-on-Action as a framework to build it. ”
P3 noted how unexpected suggestions expanded creative thinking: “ Some of the options were a bit out of the blue even, as those made me realize the amount of flexibility I had in editing, when I would only usually consider an L/J cut difference of only a second. ”
Editing is inherently creative, and there is no fixed ground truth. Still, we observed that when cut-on-action is a strong cue, timelines often show close alignment between manual and MicroEditor workflows. For example, the final cut in the Anesthesia scene resulted in nearly identical offsets across both methods. Appendix A provides a visual comparison of these timelines alongside the system’s internal synchrony analysis.
blocks.zh:
Cut-on-Operation: Cut-on-Operation标记 (中间值 7.0/7) 将乏味的帧级搜索转化为离散选择 (F2 ).
五常指出:“削减行动建议经历了一个艰难的过程,不得不找到每个大型行动的时刻,并将其与另一段剪辑相匹配,并且非常简单,非常准确。 “
P1描述了决策疲劳的减少:“只是有标记可以选择,有助于防止决策疲劳。 当你有这么多的框 和三个选项, 它帮助你缩小它。 “
在研究2中,P4描述了使用标语进行叙事:“我利用这个特征帮助我对每个场景的视频叙事采取总体方法。 如果有一个我想实现的叙述性目标,我用“停止行动”作为建立这个目标的框架。 “
P3指出,出乎意料的建议如何扩大了创造性思维:“有些选择甚至有点出乎意料,因为这些选择使我意识到我在编辑方面的灵活性,而我通常只考虑L/J的切分差只有一秒钟。 “
编辑本身就具有创造性,没有固定的事实。 尽管如此,我们仍注意到,当切入行动是一个强有力的提示时,时间表往往显示手动和微编辑工作流程之间的紧密一致。 例如,麻醉场景中的最后切口导致两种方法的抵消几乎相同。 附 录 A在系统内部同步分析的同时,对这些时间表进行了直观比较。

blocks.en:
Blink Markers: Blink markers were rated 5.5/7 in Study 1 and 4.5/7 in Study 2 (medians); they were the only feature to receive a rating below 3 (one editor), and no other feature was rated below 4, as only 4 of 16 editors across both studies reported using cut-before-blink in their regular workflow.
P3 explained when they matter: “ When everything is technically right, but it doesn’t feel like the cut is right… I use the blink. ”
P5 found them useful for pacing: “ Using [blink] I was able to keep track of the rhythm of blinking… very helpful in terms of pacing. ”
Across the remaining tools, Study 2 ratings were consistent with Study 1, confirming these findings with a larger and more diverse participant pool (Table 1 ).
blocks.zh:
闪烁标记 : Brink标记在"研究一"被评为5.5/7分,"研究二"(medians)被评为4.5/7分;它们是唯一获得低于3分(一个编辑)的特征,其他特征没有被评为低于4分,因为所有这两份研究中只有16名编辑在正常工作流程中使用剪接前链接报告.
P3解释当它们重要时:"当一切都在技术上是正确的, 我用闪烁。 “
P5发现它们对于节奏来说很有用:"使用[blink]我能够跟踪眨眼的节奏...... 在速度上很有帮助 “
在整个剩余工具中,第2项研究的评级与第1项研究一致,参与者群更大、更多样化(表1)。

Stacked icons indicate consecutive repeated operations. The top group (P1–P5) edited Pumpkin Princess with MicroEditor; the bottom group (P6–P8, P10) edited Anesthesia with MicroEditor (P9’s log was not recorded due to a logging error). blocks.en:
Exploration and Iteration: Participants rated exploration highly (median 6.0/7) and agreed the system encouraged trying different cuts (median 6.5/7).
P5 noted that suggestions led to discoveries: “ Suggestions came up; I began to think about different edits and ended up choosing several of them. ”
P2 added: “ Seeing those options does help… Otherwise I would be too rooted in my own interpretation. ”
blocks.zh:
勘探和迭代:与会者高度评价勘探(中间点为6.0/7),并同意该制度鼓励尝试不同的削减(中间点为6.5/7)。
五常指出,建议导致发现:“有人提出建议;我开始考虑不同的编辑,最后选择其中的几个。 “
P2又说:“看到这些选项确实有助于......。 否则,我将过于根植于我自己的解释。 “

blocks.en:
Participants also requested better support for finding and inserting reaction shots, which required tedious scrubbing through footage ( F5 ).
Based on this feedback, we added a Reaction Shot Browser for Study 2.
blocks.zh:
与会者还要求为发现和插入反应镜头提供更好的支持,这需要通过镜头(F5)进行乏味的清洗。
基于这些反馈,我们为研究2增加了反应相片浏览器.

blocks.en:
Reaction Shots: The Reaction Shot Browser was the highest-rated feature (median 7.0/7; 9/10 rated 7/7; DG2 ).
Editors described it as “ Emotionally satisfying ” (P7), perspective-expanding (P4: “ I never really used reaction shots as often as I could have, however, this system opened up a perspective ”), and helpful for “ break[ing] the homogeneity of long dialogues ” (P5).
Editors used reactions both for masking jump cuts from rhythm tightening (P3, P4, P8, P9) and for directing attention toward the listener’s emotional response.
P7 discovered unexpected narrative possibilities: “ Some of the reaction shots created new meanings (for example, one character’s body language slumping in a chair) which influenced the choice of what shot to end the scene with ” ( DG1 ).
The system supports two complementary insertion methods: highlighting a phrase in the interactive transcript to select semantically meaningful moments, or navigating the playhead for frame-level precision.
P2 noted that “ the dialogue highlighting feature was also helpful in finding the right time to add a clip. ”
blocks.zh:
反应相片:反应相片浏览器是最高分的特征(中间为7.0/7;9/10分为7/7;DG2.
编辑们将其描述为“情感满意”(P7),视角扩展(P4:“我从未真正使用过尽可能频繁的反应镜头,但这一系统打开了一个视角......”),并有助于“打破长对话的同质性......”(P5)。
编辑们将反应用于掩盖节奏收紧(P3,P4,P8,P9)的跳跃剪接,以及将注意力引向听众的情绪反应.
P7发现了出乎意料的叙事可能性: " 某些反应镜头创造了新的意义(例如,一个角色的身体语言在椅子上倒下),这影响了选择用什么镜头来结束场景. " (DG1).
系统支持两种互补的插入方法:在交互式记录片中突出一个短语来选择具有分解意义的瞬间,或者将播放头用于帧级精度.
P2指出,“强调这一特点的对话也有助于找到增加一个短片的适当时机。 “

blocks.en: Perceived Effort and Output: Across both studies, participants strongly agreed that MicroEditor improved their efficiency (median 7.0/7) and enjoyment (median 7.0/7). Editors also felt the assisted workflow was worth the effort and produced satisfying edits (median 6.0/7 for both). Participants reported better decision support (median 6.0/7 in both studies) and, in Study 2, higher confidence in their editing choices (median 6.0/7 vs. 5.0/7 in Study 1). In Study 2, participants felt the assisted edits improved the video output over the rough cut (median 6.0/7). P5 noted “ the pacing with [MicroEditor] resulted in a much more flowing sequence, ” and P7 found “ pacing and flow are better and easier, and save time to iterate and adjust. ” An interactive gallery of video outputs across diverse scenes, including direct comparisons to the initial rough cuts, is available on our project page.
blocks.zh: 所了解的 " 努力与产出 " :在两项研究中,与会者都强烈同意, " 微型编辑器 " 提高了效率(中间值7.0/7)和 " 享受 " (中间值7.0/7)。 编辑们还认为,辅助工作流程值得付出努力,并制作了令人满意的编辑(两者的中间点为6.0/7)。 与会者报告了更好的决策支持(两次研究的中间点为6.0/7),在研究2中,对编辑选择的信心提高(研究1中的中间点为6.0/7对5.0/7)。 在研究2中,与会者认为,辅助编辑改进了视频产出,而不是粗略剪接(中间点6.0/7)。 五常指出,“与[微编辑 的相去甚快,导致流动顺序大得多,......”和七常发现,“速度和流动更好、更容易,并节省了时间来调整和调整......”。 我们的项目网页上有一个跨不同场景的视频产出互动画廊,包括直接比较最初的粗略削减。

blocks.en:
Quantitative Analysis: To complement the qualitative findings, we analyzed the interaction logs from Study 2 ( N = 9 N=9 ; see above) to understand how the assisted tools changed editing behavior.
Table 2 summarizes the key interaction metrics across conditions.
blocks.zh:
定量分析: 为了补充定性结论,我们分析了研究2(N=9 N=9;见上文)的交互日志,以了解辅助工具如何改变编辑行为。
表2总结了各种条件的关键互动指标。

blocks.en:
We logged all timeline operations, distinguishing between manual operations (direct clip trims, drags, repositioning) and assisted operations (rhythm edits, applying cut offset suggestions, and inserting reaction shots).
Reaction shot selection uses a modal gallery interface with its own filtering and preview controls, so we report time in this interface separately (RS in Table 2 ).
blocks.zh:
我们记录了所有的时间线操作,区分手动操作(直接剪接,拖放,再定位)和辅助操作(韵律编辑,应用剪切抵消建议,并插入反应镜头).
反应相片选择使用带有自有过滤和预览控件的模式画廊接口,因此我们在此接口中单独报告时间(RS in Table 2 .).

blocks.en:
Our formative study found that micro-editing involves tedious frame-by-frame work ( F1 ).
With MicroEditor , all nine participants shifted from low-level timeline manipulation to structured tool interactions, with fewer total operations needed to achieve their edits (Table 2 ).
All nine showed a lower operation rate (mean 1.4 vs. 4.9 Ops/min, sign test p = 0.004 p=0.004 , Cohen’s d = − 1.57 d=-1.57 ), suggesting that the tools compressed what would otherwise require many fine-grained manual adjustments into fewer, higher-level actions.
Although participants perceived the tools as reducing effort (P9: “ If I were to manually edit, I would be using fewer cuts for awkward silences just because of the manual labor that went into each cut ”, P3: “ T replaces a lot of clunky movement selecting clips and moving them ”), MicroEditor sessions were not shorter on average (13.1 vs. 11.4 min). Editors appear to have reinvested the reduced mechanical effort into exploring more alternatives, including an average of 3.6 minutes browsing the reaction shot gallery, a modality that does not exist in the baseline condition. Because this additional exploration time makes raw duration comparisons between conditions difficult to interpret, we report operation rates (Ops/min) as the primary measure of mechanical effort.
In the baseline condition, participants were given freeform editing instructions with no requirement to add reaction shots. Despite this, three participants (P6, P7, P8) chose to manually create reaction shots by extending portions of neighboring clips and moving them to the B-roll track. With MicroEditor, the Reaction Shot Browser replaced this manual search entirely. Baseline session times therefore likely undercount the effort needed to search through all available footage for ideal reaction shots. As P2 reflected, without the tools “ it took a lot of time and I couldn’t easily add additional reaction clips. ” Under time pressure, editors resort to nearby clips instead. P6 noted, “ Usually I would grab a reaction right before and after if I’m in a time crunch. ”
blocks.zh:
我们的成型研究发现,微观编辑涉及一个个地乏味的工作(F1)。

blocks.en:
Exploration Patterns: Beyond aggregate counts, the interaction logs reveal how participants used the assisted tools.
Following prior analyses of creative tool usage patterns ( Masson et al., 2025 ) , Figure 8 illustrates the full operation sequence for each participant.
Eight of nine participants began their sessions with rhythm edits ( F3 ), adjusting pacing by feel before moving to cut offset suggestions ( F4 ) and reaction shots ( F5 ). This ordering is consistent with our formative study, where editors described addressing rhythm before visual attention. P3 was the sole exception, skipping rhythm edits entirely, likely because the rough cut’s existing pacing already suited their creative intent.
Seven of nine participants also exhibited iterative refinement at individual cut points, applying a cut offset suggestion, previewing the result in context, resetting, and trying a different suggestion before committing.
Three participants (P1, P2, P8) compared across rule types at the same cut, for example applying a cut-on-action suggestion, resetting, then trying a character-focus suggestion, evaluating how different editorial rationales felt in practice.
Usage patterns varied widely. P3 completed the entire session with only 5 assisted operations (3 cut offset suggestions applied, 2 reaction shots inserted), relying entirely on the system’s defaults. P8, the most active explorer, touched every cut point, compared multiple rule types, and inserted 9 reaction shots across 40 total operations.
Similar iterative apply-preview-reset patterns have been observed across other creative domains ( Smith et al., 2025 ) .

blocks.en: 7. Discussion
blocks.zh: 7. 联合国 讨论情况

blocks.en: Our evaluations focused on how well MicroEditor supports our design goals. In this section, we discuss transferable insights from our design (Section 7.1 ), how our tools changed the way editors explored (Section 7.2 ), and limitations and future work (Section 7.3 ).
blocks.zh: 我们的评价侧重于微编辑如何支持我们的设计目标。 在本节中,我们讨论从设计(第7.1节)中可转移的见解、我们的工具如何改变编辑探索的方式(第7.2节)以及限制和今后的工作(第7.3节)。

blocks.en: 7.1. Discretizing Continuous Creative Spaces
blocks.zh: 7.1. 分散持续创造性空间

blocks.en: The space of possible micro-edits is continuous: audio and video cuts can be decoupled by any offset within W W{}{} . It is also multidimensional, since each cut involves competing objectives like rhythm, character emphasis, and action continuity. Editors reason about this space through discrete heuristics instead: cut-on-action, cut-before-blink, favor a character’s screen time. Our core contribution is turning these heuristics into navigable structures built on audiovisual synchrony windows, which serve two purposes at once. For the editor, they guarantee perceptual safety: any offset within W ​ v W{}{v} preserves audiovisual flow, so the editor can focus on creative intent instead of watching for lip-sync errors. For the system, they shrink the AI’s search space, limiting the frames a VLM must reason about to a region where every candidate is already valid. Recent work calls this kind of shared structure a compositional substrate ( Cao et al., 2025 ) . It makes both the human’s and the AI’s work interpretable to each other. Our system goes further by populating these windows with categorized alternatives, so they become a structure for composition, not a boundary that excludes bad options. The same idea applies to reaction shots, where low-synchrony regions become candidates the system indexes by emotion and shot size for browsing ( F5 ).
blocks.zh: 可能微编辑的空间是连续的: 音频和视频剪接可以被WQQ内部的任何抵消去除. 它也是多层面的,因为每项削减都涉及节奏、性格强调和行动连续性等相互竞争的目标。 编辑器通过离散的电流来解释这个空间:切入动作,切入前链接,偏好字符的屏幕时间. 我们的核心贡献是将这些热能转化为可导航的结构,这种结构建立在视听同步窗口上,同时服务于两个目的。 对编辑来说,它们保证了知觉安全:W v W{}{v}内部的任何抵消都保留了视听流,因此编辑可以专注于创造性意图,而不必关注唇音同步错误. 对这个系统来说, 他们缩小了AI的搜索空间, 将 VLM 的帧限制在每一个候选人都已经有效的区域。 最近的工作将这种共享结构称为构成地基(Cao等,2025年)。 它使人类和大赦国际的工作相互解释。 我们的系统更进一步,将这些窗口添加到分类的替代品中,这样它们就成为一个组成结构,而不是排除不良选项的界限。 同样的想法也适用于反应镜头,低同步区域通过情绪和镜头大小成为系统索引候选人来浏览(F5.

blocks.en: More broadly, this suggests three design principles for creativity support in continuous perceptual parameter spaces, such as photo and video color grading or character animation: • Formalize domain constraints to compute boundaries within which any choice is perceptually safe. • Within those boundaries, surface alternatives categorized by domain-specific rationale rather than ranked by a single score. • A single computed constraint can serve more than one purpose: the same boundary that defines when one operation is safe can also define candidates for a complementary operation. We demonstrate these principles in film micro-editing, but they should apply more broadly. In AI-assisted photo color grading, for instance, perceptual constraints (skin tones stay natural, highlights do not clip) could define safe boundaries within which generated alternatives are grouped by aesthetic intent rather than ranked by a single quality score. In character animation, the same skeletal rig that keeps a motion perceptually plausible also lets an animator reuse it, like walking, across many different characters. Applying a motion template like this, instead of tuning each joint’s rotation knobs one by one, turns a continuous space of poses into multiple, easy-to-navigate discrete choices.
blocks.zh: 更广义地说,这提出了在相片和视频色彩分级或人物动画等连续感知参数空间中创造性支持的三项设计原则: • 正式化域限制来计算任何选择在概念上都是安全的边界. 二. 支助 在这些界限内,表层替代品按具体领域的理由分类,而不是单分。 二. 支助 一个单一的计算限制可以服务于一个以上的目的:确定一个行动何时安全时的同一边界也可以确定补充行动的候选人. 我们在电影的微型编辑中展示了这些原则,但这些原则应更广泛地适用。 例如,在人工智能辅助的相片彩色分级中,知觉限制(皮肤色素保持自然,亮点不剪接)可以界定安全界限,其中生成的替代品按审美意图分组,而不是按单一质量分数排序。 在角色动画中,保持运动感知的同一块骨架也让动画师像行走一样再利用它来跨越许多不同的角色. 应用这样的一个运动模板,而不是将每个关节的旋转接子一个接一个地调取,将一个连续的摆放空间变成多个容易实现的离散选择.

blocks.en: Formalize domain constraints to compute boundaries within which any choice is perceptually safe.
blocks.zh: 正式确定域限制,以计算任何选择在概念上都是安全的边界。

blocks.en: Within those boundaries, surface alternatives categorized by domain-specific rationale rather than ranked by a single score.
blocks.zh: 在这些界限内,表层替代品按具体领域的理由分类,而不是单分。

blocks.en: A single computed constraint can serve more than one purpose: the same boundary that defines when one operation is safe can also define candidates for a complementary operation.
blocks.zh: 一个单一的计算限制可以服务于一个以上的目的:确定一个行动何时安全时的同一边界也可以确定补充行动的候选人.

blocks.en: 7.2. Lowering the Cost of Exploration
blocks.zh: 7.2. 降低勘探费用

blocks.en: Because any point within W W{} is perceptually safe, the system can surface multiple discrete suggestions at each cut, categorized by editorial rationale, and populate a reaction shot browser from low-synchrony regions in the source footage. This categorization is a deliberate design choice. A single “best” AI output often induces design fixation ( Wadinambiarachchi et al., 2024 ) , and when AI auto-fills an entire structure, the perceived cost of revision stifles exploration ( Cao et al., 2025 ) . To avoid premature convergence, our approach explicitly extracts dimensions (editorial rationales) across which users can explore alternatives, making the continuous design space legible rather than merely navigable ( Suh et al., 2024 ) .
blocks.zh: 由于W-QQ内部的任何一点在感知上都是安全的,系统可以在每次剪接时浮出多个离散的建议,按照编辑原理分类,并从源片段的低同步区域中填入一个反应镜头浏览器. 这种分类是一种有意的设计选择。 单一的“最佳”AI输出往往诱发设计固定(Wadinambiarachchi等,2024年),当AI自动填充整个结构时,所意识到的修改成本会抑制探索(Cao等,2025年)。 为了避免过早的趋同,我们的方法明确提取了用户可以探索替代品的维度(编辑原理),使连续设计空间可以辨别,而不仅仅是通航(Suh等,2024年)。

blocks.en: The interaction logs suggest this strategy worked: participants compared suggestions drawn from different rationales at the same cut point before committing (Figure 8 ), a rapid comparison that depends on alternatives being computationally and interactively cheap ( Huh et al., 2025 ) . By never auto-applying suggestions, our system lets editors try with one click and revert with another ( DG2 ).
blocks.zh: 互动记录表明,这一战略行之有效:与会者在承诺之前的同一个切入点比较了不同理由提出的建议(图8),这种快速比较取决于替代品的计算和互动成本(Huh等人,2025年)。 我们的系统从不自动应用建议,让编辑者尝试一次,然后返回一次(DG2)。

blocks.en:
The quantitative logs tell the same story at a broader scale. All nine logged participants showed a lower operation rate with MicroEditor than in the baseline (Table 2 ), a shift from frame-level adjustments to higher-level creative evaluations.


Lowering the cost per attempt did not make sessions shorter. Instead, editors spent the saved mechanical effort on trying more alternatives, an instance of what Olsen (2007) calls expressive leverage . When a tool is effective, it does more than speed up standard tasks. It changes what creators choose to do ( Shneiderman et al., 2006 ) .


P6 explained: “ when you’re on a time crunch, you don’t care that much… you just go with the first thing you see that works. But here… the cost of trying is a lot lower ” ( DG1 ).
blocks.zh:
定量日志以更广阔的尺度讲述同一故事. 所有9名登录的参与者在微编辑器上的操作率都低于基线(表2),从帧级调整转向更高级别的创造性评价。


降低每次尝试的费用不会缩短会期。 编辑们将节省下来的机械精力花在尝试更多替代品上, 当一个工具有效时,它所做的不仅仅是加快标准任务. 它改变了创作者选择做什么(Shneiderman等,2006年).


P6解释道:"当你处于时间紧缩状态时, 你只是去的第一件事 你看到它的工作。 但这里... 尝试的成本要低得多......”(DG1)。

blocks.en:
The tedious part of micro-editing is finding viable candidates, not choosing between them. Dmytryk et al. (2018) makes the same distinction: editors settle for simpler cuts when better ones take “more time and greater effort,” yet the cut itself depends on a sense of timing that defines exceptional editors. We see the same pattern here: once search became cheap, editors used techniques they already knew more often, but still made every timing decision themselves. This points to where automation belongs in creative tools: the search that comes before a decision.


Automating the search while preserving the choice respects the expertise that editors bring to every cut.
blocks.zh:
乏味的微编辑部分是寻找可行的候选人,而不是在他们之间做出选择. Dmytryk等人(2018年)也做出了同样的区分:编辑们在更好的剪辑需要“更多时间和更大的努力”时会决定更简单的剪辑方式,然而剪辑本身则取决于界定杰出编辑的时间安排。 我们在这里看到同样的模式:一旦搜索变得便宜,编辑们就使用他们已经更经常地知道的技术,但仍会自己决定每一个时间。 这说明自动化在创意工具中属于哪里:在决定前的搜索.


自动搜索同时保留选择,尊重编辑员给每个剪接带来的专门知识.

blocks.en: 7.3. Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 7.3. 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en: Model Dependencies: Our system relies on off-the-shelf models for synchrony estimation (LR-ASD, AVID-CMA), blink detection (MediaPipe), and a VLM (Gemini 3.0 Flash) for coarse scene analysis and cut-on-action suggestions via numbered mosaics, and is bounded by their current capabilities. Current VLMs lack fine-grained temporal understanding ( Qu et al., 2025 ) . Synchrony models can also struggle with multiple simultaneous speakers or overlapping dialogue, and we assume a single mixed audio track. These models are pluggable components in our formalization rather than contributions of their own, so improvements to any of them would improve the system directly, without changing the interaction design.
blocks.zh: 模型依赖: 我们的系统依靠现成的模型进行同步估计(LR-ASD,AVID-CMA),眨眼探测(MediaPipe),和VLM(Gemini 3.0 Flash)进行粗糙的场景分析和通过编号的镶嵌来切入操作的建议,并以它们目前的能力相接. 目前的VLM缺乏精细的时间理解(Qu等,2025.). 同步模式也可以与多个同步的扬声器或相重叠的对话相抗争,我们假设一个单一的混合音频音轨. 这些模型在我们的正式化中是可插接的组件,而不是它们自己的贡献,所以对其中任何一个模型的改进都会直接改善系统,而不改变交互设计.

blocks.en: Scope and Generalization: Our implementation and evaluation focus on dialogue scenes. Scene types where synchrony plays a smaller role (voiceovers, music-driven scenes, or action scenes without dialogue) would require new definitions of synchrony and rhythm, which we leave to future work. The value of micro-editing also depends on the starting rough cut, and there is no single ground-truth final cut: editing styles varied widely even among our participants (Figure 8 , Table 2 ). Finally, our formalization treats each micro-edit as a local decision, but editors may want consistency across cuts, such as cutting consistently early or late on speaker changes. Conditioning suggestions on an editor’s prior decisions is another direction for future work.
blocks.zh: 范围和普遍性: 我们的执行和评价侧重于对话场景。 同步起较小作用的场景类型(语音翻唱,由音乐驱动的场景,或没有对话的动作场景)需要同步和节奏的新定义,我们留给未来工作. 微编辑的价值也取决于开始的粗略剪接,而且没有单一的地情最终剪接:编辑风格即使在我们的参与者中也大相径庭(图8,表2)。 最后,我们的正规化将每个微编辑视为地方决定,但编辑们可能希望各行各业保持一致,如在演讲者更改时总是及早剪接或迟剪接。 就编辑先前的决定提出附加条件的建议是今后工作的另一个方向。

blocks.en: Informing Agentic and Generative Video Tools: Current generative video models produce tightly synchronized audio-video outputs with no mechanism for the audiovisual decoupling that professional editors rely on to control pacing and attention. Our formalization of the micro-edit space provides a structure for future AI systems. By applying these synchrony bounds, both agentic editing tools and video models could produce outputs with explicit rhythm and view control, bridging micro-editing and macro-editing.
blocks.zh: 告知代理和基因视频工具 : 目前的基因视频模型产生紧凑同步的音频视频输出,没有专业编辑依靠的音频脱钩机制来控制速度和注意力. 我们微编辑空间的正式化为未来的AI系统提供了一个结构. 通过应用这些同步边框,代理编辑工具和视频模型都可以以明确的节奏和取景控制,连接微编辑和宏编辑输出出产出.

blocks.en: 8. Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8. 结论

blocks.en:
While rough cuts establish a film’s narrative, the transition to a polished fine cut requires navigating a continuous, multidimensional space of micro-edits that has previously remained informal and manual. Our work formalizes this stage by decoupling audio and video through synchrony windows , transforming a tedious, frame-by-frame process into a structured computational space. By surfacing specific micro-edit types, from rhythm control to viewer attention (cut-on-action, cut-before-blink, and reaction-shot alternatives), we provide a representation that bridges the gap between raw timeline operations and the editor’s intent.
Editors in our studies reported that this structure reduced mechanical effort and allowed them to reinvest their focus into higher-level creative goals.
More broadly, this work demonstrates that computational assistance in creative workflows is most effective when it operates at this intermediate granularity: providing the structure to navigate complex decision spaces without automating the creative outcome.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en: Appendix A Qualitative Timeline Comparisons
blocks.zh: 附录A 定性时间线比较

blocks.en:
This appendix visualizes the final timelines for the Anesthesia scene to compare the baseline manual workflow (P1) with MicroEditor (P6). As noted in Section 6.2, micro-editing is subjective. Overall pacing and reaction shot placements naturally vary based on individual editing styles.
However, when perceptual cues are strong, we observe similar timing outcomes. Figure 9 shows both participants arriving at a comparable J-cut offset (0.9s vs. 1.1s) near the end of the scene, driven by a cut-on-action.
To illustrate the underlying method that generates these suggestions, Figure 10 provides a detailed view of the system’s internal synchrony model for the same Anesthesia scene. It visualizes the word-level ASR alignments, the continuous audio-visual synchrony curves ( σ \sigma ), and the resulting calculated bounds that constrain the suggestions surfaced in UI.
blocks.zh:
本附录可视化了麻醉场景的最终时长,将基线手动工作流程(P1)与微编辑器(P6)进行比较. 正如第6.2节所指出,微观编辑是主观的。 整体的相位和反应相片投放会根据个人编辑风格而自然而然地有所不同.

blocks.en: This section details the offline preprocessing that extracts the signals used by the interactive tools described in Section 5 . Given source footage 𝐌 \mathbf{M{}}{} and a rough cut 𝐑 \mathbf{R}{} , preprocessing runs in three stages before the editing session begins (Figure 4 ).

blocks.en: B.1. System Implementation and Prompt Details
blocks.zh: B.1. 系统实施和快速细节

blocks.en: Since VLMs excel at coarse scene understanding but struggle with micro-temporal reasoning due to their inherent sparse sampling ( Qu et al., 2025 ) , we use VLMs for semantic analysis (character identification, shot classification) while relying on traditional computer vision for frame-level signals (synchrony proxy, blink detection).
blocks.zh: 由于VLMs在粗糙的场景理解上表现优异,但由于其固有的零星采样(Qu等,2025年)而与微时推理相搏,所以我们使用VLM来进行语义分析(特征识别,镜头分类),同时依靠传统的计算机视觉来进行帧级信号(同步代理,眨眼检测).

blocks.en: Stage 1: VLM Coarse Analysis (2–5 min): A VLM (Gemini) analyzes all source footage sampled at 1 FPS to within 1 API call to cross-associate semantic information and produce a global character map . For each source clip M j ∈ 𝐌 M{}_{j}\in\mathbf{M{}}{} , the VLM identifies distinct characters, shot types, and non-usable regions. We use 480p proxy files to reduce token cost while preserving sufficient detail for character recognition. The prompt structure:
blocks.zh: 第1阶段:VLM粗细分析(2–5分):AVLM(Gemini)分析1个FPS所采样到1个API内的所有源片段,调取跨关联语义信息并制作全局字符图. 每个源剪辑 M j QQ M{}_{j}\in\ mathbf{M{}}{}],VLM识别出不同的字符,镜头类型,以及无法使用的区域. 我们使用 480p 代理文件来降低符号成本,同时保留足够的细节来识别字符. 即时结构:

blocks.en: Analyze ALL footage files together to identify characters and shot types. CHARACTER IDENTIFICATION: Identify all distinct people and objects of interest across all footage files (Figure 11 ). The same person in different footage = same character_id. Look for: hair, clothing, glasses, facial features, body type. A close-up in one footage and wide shot in another can be the same person. SHOT TYPE CLASSIFICATION: Classify each segment as: extreme_close_up, close_up, medium_close_up, medium, medium_wide, wide, over_the_shoulder, two_shot, or group_shot. OVER-THE-SHOULDER RULE: In OTS shots, assign character_id to the person whose face is visible (not the person shown from behind). This ensures visible faces for reaction shot extraction. NON-USABLE SEGMENTS: Mark slates, crew visible, camera movement, and empty frames as no_character. TEMPORAL COVERAGE: Cover the entire duration of each footage file with no gaps. Approximate timing ( ± \pm 1–2 seconds) is acceptable.

SHOT TYPE 分类法:将每个片段分类为: 极地-接近地-接近地-接近地-接近地-接近地-接近地-接近地-中等地-接近地-接近地-,介质-宽地-宽地-过地-肩地-,双地-射地-或群地-射地. {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}我们得谈谈 在OTS shots中,将字符_id指定给面相可见的人(而不是从后方显示的人). 这保证了反应镜头取出时的可见面. 不可使用部分: 标出板块,机组可见,相机移动,和空框为无字符. 临时覆盖: 覆盖每个片段文件的整个持续时间,没有空白. 大致时间(±\pm 1–2秒)是可以接受的.

blocks.en: Stage 3: VLM-ASD Correspondence (instant): We link VLM character identities to ASD face tracks by extracting representative face crops from each track and querying Gemini to match them against VLM-generated character thumbnails. When matching is ambiguous, we fall back to DeepFace embeddings (Facenet512) with cosine similarity. This enables per-character queries of σ \sigma{} and supports the character focus optimization (Section 5.3 ).

blocks.en: B.2. Cut-on-Action Detection
blocks.zh: B.2. 停止行动探测

blocks.en: Current state of VLMs cannot reliably reason about frame-level motion continuity ( Qu et al., 2025 ) . We address this by converting the temporal reasoning problem into a spatial matching task. The model is prompted with the 2 × \times 2 grid layout (sample from the left and right bounds of W W ) and temporal alignment rules:
blocks.zh: 目前VLMs的状态无法可靠地说明帧级运动连续性的理由(Qu等,2025.). 我们通过将时间推理问题转化为空间匹配任务来解决这个问题。 该模型由2×x\times 2网格布局(从W W的左右边界取出样本)和时间对接规则所推动:

blocks.en: You are a professional film editor with expertise in cut-on-action techniques. GRID LAYOUT: Top row shows earlier cut opportunities (outgoing end, incoming preroll). Bottom row shows later cut opportunities (outgoing post-roll, incoming start). TEMPORAL ALIGNMENT RULES: • For later cuts (J-cut): Match frames with equal numbers (A=B), since frame 1 = cut point for both grids. • For earlier cuts (L-cut): Match frames by distance from last frame, maintaining consistent offset (B − - A). FOCUS ON: Motion trajectory, direction continuity, body alignment (head angle, shoulder rotation, limb positions), and temporal alignment.
blocks.zh: 你是一位专业的电影编辑,擅长切入动作技术. GRID LAYOUT:上行显示更早的剪接机会(出行结束,入行预卷). 下行显示以后剪接机会(出后卷,入后起). • 以后的削减(J-剪接): 匹配等号的帧(A=B),因为帧 1 = 两个网格的切入点. 二. 支助 先前的削减(L-剪接): 以相距上个相距相匹配帧,保持相容偏移(B−-A). FOCUS ON:运动轨迹,方向连续性,身体对接(头角,肩部自转,四肢位置),以及时间对接.

blocks.zh: 以后的削减( J- cut) : 匹配等号的帧(A=B),因为帧 1=两个网格的切入点.

blocks.en: For earlier cuts (L-cut): Match frames by distance from last frame, maintaining consistent offset (B − - A).
blocks.zh: 先前的削减(L-剪接): 以相距上个相距相匹配帧,保持相容偏移(B−-A).

blocks.en: C.2. Study Format
blocks.zh: C.2. 学习格式

blocks.en: All participants completed a 60-minute in-person session. After a tutorial on MicroEditor terminology and features, participants edited two 1-minute dialogue scenes using our interface: “Pumpkin Princess” (awkward romantic interaction between a nerdy outcast and her crush) and “Anesthesia” (suspenseful 1950s scene where a housewife suspects her dentist). Participants completed both conditions in counterbalanced order: manual editing (all features disabled) and assisted editing (features enabled). We encouraged think-aloud protocol throughout. Following each edit, participants rated features on 7-point Likert scales and completed creativity support metrics adapted from the Creativity Support Index (Table 5 ).
